verdict.rationale: Cua describes itself as open-source infrastructure. Its docs say any machine running cua-spacesd (a spare Mac, a LAN server, or a VM in your own cloud) can host Spaces and be reached directly by address and env token. The SDK runs locally on Docker/Podman/QEMU/Lume, needs no account to start, and a community user reports running Lume locally to sandbox Claude. Missing for 10: documentation for self-hosting the relay and team/admin coordination layer, licensing details for every component, and independent hands-on reports of self-hosting the Spaces daemon specifically.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Open source infrastructure for computer use agents: Cua Spaces, Cua Driver, Lume, the Cua SDK and Cua Bench.
Any machine that runs cua-spacesd, such as a spare Mac, a server on your LAN or Tailscale... connects directly by address and env token.
Connect a Mac on your desk, a spare box in the office or a VM in your own AWS, Google Cloud or Modal account. Each one runs Spaces
the SDK uses Docker or Podman (gVisor when installed), QEMU, or Lume on Apple silicon. Any OCI image works.
